metadata.purpose: Normalized coverage knowledge for the CFB 27 coordinator recommendation/read engine.
principles: Coverage labels describe families, not guarantees; match/rotation rules can change after the snap.
Pre-snap indicators are clues, not proof. Prefer post-snap confirmation when available.
A concept being listed as a stress point does not mean it automatically wins.
EA/CFB gameplay observations and real-football coaching rules are tracked separately when possible.

cover_0.structure: Man coverage with no dedicated deep middle safety; commonly paired with pressure.
pre_snap_indicators: No true deep-middle safety or safeties walked down.
Defenders aligned with obvious man leverage across eligible receivers.
Pressure body count can exceed the offense's available blockers.
post_snap_confirmation: Coverage defenders carry receivers immediately with little or no deep help.
One or more second-level/secondary defenders add to the rush.
risk_notes: The ball must usually come out quickly; long-developing concepts can expose protection.

cover_1.structure: Man coverage underneath with a deep middle safety; some variants add a robber/hole defender.
pre_snap_indicators: Corners/overhangs often align with receiver leverage consistent with man responsibilities.
Motion can help reveal defenders traveling with receivers.
post_snap_confirmation: Deep safety remains over the middle; a robber variant may cut intermediate routes.
risk_notes: Robber/hole variants can punish blindly throwing in-breakers into the middle.

cover_2_man.structure: Two deep safeties over man coverage underneath.
pre_snap_indicators: Underneath defenders aligned tightly enough to carry receivers in man.
post_snap_confirmation: Underneath defenders turn and carry receivers rather than spot-dropping.
Two safeties remain high over the top.
stress_points: QB scramble space if rush lanes open
risk_notes: Deep shots are capped by two safeties unless leverage is decisively won.

cover_2.structure: Two deep-half defenders with underneath defenders handling flats/hooks/curls.
pre_snap_indicators: Corners may show flatter or squat leverage compared with quarters/man.
post_snap_confirmation: Safeties divide the deep field into halves.
Corners/underneath defenders relate to flat and hook/curl zones.
risk_notes: Cover 2 Read/pattern-match variants can remove classic static-zone answers.

cover_3.structure: Three deep defenders divide the deep field into thirds with underneath zone/match responsibilities.
pre_snap_indicators: Often presents one-high structure, though rotation can disguise it.
post_snap_confirmation: Corners and middle safety form three deep thirds.
Four underneath defenders distribute curl/flat/hook areas in common variants.
risk_notes: Pattern-match Cover 3 variants can carry vertical routes differently from spot-drop Cover 3.

cover_4.structure: Four deep defenders protect quarters of the field; many real systems pattern-match routes rather than spot-drop.
pre_snap_indicators: Two-high shell with corners/safeties positioned to handle vertical threats.
post_snap_confirmation: Both safeties remain involved vertically rather than rotating to a single-high middle.
Corners/safeties may match eligible vertical releases.
risk_notes: Do not assume static four-zone behavior; quarters rules frequently become man-like on vertical releases.

cover_6.structure: Split-field coverage combining quarters principles to one side with Cover 2/half-field principles to the other.
pre_snap_indicators: Usually presents a two-high shell; corner leverage may differ by side.
post_snap_confirmation: One side behaves like quarters while the other behaves like a Cover 2 half.
Read the concept side independently rather than treating the coverage as symmetric.
risk_notes: Advice must account for which side is quarters and which side is half-field; shell alone is insufficient.
